The State Government is on appeal challenging the judgment and order dated 30.01.2012 passed by the Additional District Judge, (Fast Track Court), Chitradurga in M.A.(LAC) No.23/2011, by which M.A(LAC) No.23/2011 was dismissed and the order passed by the Reference Court in R.P No.1/2008 by the Senior Civil Judge, Holalkere and decree passed in LAC No.153/1978 dated 15.02.1983 was up held.
2.

entities.text: Additional District Judge, (Fast Track Court), Chitradurga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The land belonging to the respondents was acquired for the purpose of formation of house sites.
An award was passed on 15.12.1983 awarding compensation along with solatium of 15% and interest of 5%.

Later the respondents filed a R.P.No.01/2008 dated 10.12.1998 to review the judgment and award stating that they were entitled to solatium at 30% and interest at the rate of 9% for the first year from the date of taking possession and at 15% for the subsequent years till the date of payment,
as per the amended Section 23(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and 34 of the Land Acquisition Act.

The Reference Court entertained the review petition and held that the respondents were entitled to solatium at 30% and interest at the rate of 9% and 15% respectively, in view of the NC:
2023:KHC:41016 amendment to the Land Acquisition Act.

The Reference Court therefore, directed the appellant herein to pay solatium at 30% on the market value and the interest at the rate of 9%
for the first year and 15% thereafter till the date of payment of the compensation.

Being aggrieved by The Assistant Commissioner And vs B M P Basappa on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31129468/
3 the said order the appellant filed M.A(LAC) No.23/2011 primarily contending that, the respondents sought review of the reference after 20 long years.

sentences.text: It also contended that the reference Court was devoid of the powers to review orders and therefore, the impugned order passed by the Reference Court as well as the order passed by the appellate Court warrant interference.
3. Though the respondent Nos.1 and 2(e) are represented through counsel there is no appearance for them.

Be that as it may Section 23(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was amended by Act 68/84 with effect from 30.04.1982 enabling the land losers to claim solatium @ 30% and interest @ 15%
per annum.
In the present case, the award of Reference Court was admittedly passed on 15.02.1983 by which solatium @ 15% and interest @ 5% per annum was awarded.
This Judgment award was fundamentally flawed and NC: 2023:KHC:41016 deserved to be reviewed.
The respondents were entitled to the benefits that is conferred on them in accordance with law.

4. The contention of the learned High Court Government Pleader that the Reference Court had no power to review, is liable to rejected in view of the provisions contained in the Order 47 rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure which permits a review of the judgment to be entertained if the judgment and award was not in accordance with law.

The further contention that the review petition was entertained after 20 years and therefore, such a review petition could not have been considered, is also liable to be rejected in view of the purpose behind Section 28-A and the beneficial nature of the Land Acquisition Act.
In that view of the matter, there is no merit in this appeal and the same is dismissed.
4. Any amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Reference Court for appropriate orders.
